mainTopic: Redeeming consecrated and sold fields (inherited, bought, rocky fields and trees), the חומש, and fixed payments for a slave and for an אונס or מפתה
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא. רבי מאיר uses a פסוק to show that a field a son bought from his father counts as a שדה אחוזה only if the father died before the son consecrated it. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say it counts even if the father died afterward. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that they learn this from the extra word משדה, not from a rule about the time of פדיון. Next, רב פפא lists rules for rocky fields and for trees, both consecrated and sold. Each law follows the exact word in its own פסוק: זרע, שדה, תבואה or אחוזה. The גמרא then asks why consecrated trees are not redeemed together with their land, and it limits נהרדעי's rule to a buyer who claims he bought the land too. A ברייתא teaches that a שדה מקנה is redeemed at its real value, while רבי אליעזר holds it has a fixed price. רבא and a ברייתא show that by the רבנן a שדה מקנה has no חומש. Two new משניות then teach fixed Torah payments: thirty סלע for a slave killed by a שור המועד, and fifty סלע for an אונס or מפתה, with בושת and פגם added. רב זעירא's first explanation for these extra payments is knocked down by אביי, and his new answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse behind רבי מאיר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי מאיר's source: the פסוק speaks of a bought field that is not a שדה אחוזה. That leaves out a field that has already become a שדה אחוזה because the father died before it was consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'If he sanctifies a field that he bought, which is not from his ancestral field.' That means a field that is not an ancestral field. It leaves out this field, which is an ancestral field.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of a ברייתא, and רבי מאיר is giving his source from the תורה. The פסוק about consecrating a bought field only covers a field that is not a שדה אחוזה when it is consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son bought a field from his father, and then the father died, so the son now inherits it. רבי מאיר says that if the father died before the son consecrated the field, it counts as a שדה אחוזה. The words 'which is not from his ancestral field' leave out exactly that case.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. This introduces a source from a פסוק.
A field that was bought, not inherited
An ancestral (inherited) field. Its redemption rules and what happens to it at יובל are different.
This is left out (excluded) by the verse

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. When the father dies BEFORE the field is consecrated, everyone agrees it is a שדה אחוזה. The argument is only about when he consecrates FIRST and the father dies afterward.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"If [he sanctifies] a field that he has bought,
which is not of his ancestral field" —
a field that is not an ancestral field,
excludes this one, which is an ancestral field.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the field whose father died before the son consecrated it, so it was already inherited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the bought-field rules of the פסוק apply only to a field that is not a שדה אחוזה when it is consecrated.

steps.title: What is the reason of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say the field is a שדה אחוזה even if the father died after it was consecrated. The גמרא asks why, since the פסוק is already being used for רבי מאיר's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, even if he consecrated it and afterward the father died, it is an ancestral field. What is the reason? If it is because of the verse, the verse comes to teach רבי מאיר's point!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the other opinion in the ברייתא and asks what it is based on. It rules out the פסוק as their source, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their ruling goes further than רבי מאיר's: the father's death even AFTER the consecration still makes it a שדה אחוזה. The גמרא assumes the פסוק is already used for רבי מאיר's case, where the father died first, so it cannot also be their source. That means some other reason is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated it (gave the field to the בית המקדש treasury)
What is the reason?
A verse (פסוק)

phrases.english: Whereas according to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת אָב —
phrases.english: even if he consecrated it and afterward the father died —
it is an ancestral field.
What is the reason?
If it is because of the verse —
the verse comes for the teaching of Rabbi Meir!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the other opinion in the ברייתא and questions where it comes from.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון's ruling, given that the פסוק is used by רבי מאיר?

steps.title: Their reason must be that they judge by the time of redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון follow the field's status at the time of פדיון. That would show רבי שמעון goes by the redemption time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not because he follows the time of redemption?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers the only reason it can think of: these תנאים decide the field's status by how things stand when it is redeemed. This becomes a proof about רבי שמעון's general approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father died before the son redeemed the field, so at the time of פדיון it is inherited. That would make it a שדה אחוזה. If רבי שמעון always goes by the time of פדיון, the earlier claim (רב הונא's) that the ברייתא about trees and a field follows רבי שמעון falls apart. That ברייתא has them redeemed separately, not by their combined status at the time of redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that...? (introduces the reason the גמרא is driven to)
Goes after, follows
Redemption (buying the field back from הקדש)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real challenge in the sugya. It uses this ברייתא to show something about רבי שמעון's general approach to consecrated fields.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not because
he follows [the status at the time of] redemption?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by suggesting their reason is the time of redemption.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון decides a consecrated field's status by the time of redemption.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון in the ברייתא, once the פסוק has been ruled out as their source.

steps.title: They learned it from a verse instead
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון did not reason from the time of פדיון; they found a פסוק and learned their rule from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון found a verse and expounded it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back on the proof from step 3. Their ruling comes from a פסוק they explained, not from a rule about the time of redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 3 only worked because no other reason seemed possible. Once we say these תנאים learned it from a פסוק, nothing shows that רבי שמעון follows the time of פדיון. So the earlier claim that the ברייתא about trees and a field follows רבי שמעון can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: They found
And they expounded (explained the verse to learn a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge said רבי שמעון judges by the time of פדיון. It is pushed off: his ruling here comes from his reading of a פסוק, not from that general rule.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon
found a verse and expounded it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קְרָא אַשְׁכַּחוּ וּדְרוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 3 by giving these תנאים a source from a פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון follow the time of פדיון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed they had no source from a פסוק. In fact they found a פסוק and expounded it.

steps.title: The extra word משדה teaches the rule of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק shows the פסוק: the תורה could have left out the word משדה. Since it wrote it, the bought-field law covers only a field that could never become a שדה אחוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the תורה should have written 'a field he bought, which is not his ancestral.' Why does it add 'of the field'? To teach that only a field that is not fit to become an ancestral field is treated as a bought field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows the exact פסוק that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from. This finally answers the question from Step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has an extra word, משדה, that seems unneeded. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read it to mean that a bought field is redeemed by its value only if it could never become a שדה אחוזה. A field the son was going to inherit was always fit to become אחוזה, so it is redeemed like an ancestral field even if the father died after it was consecrated.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your reading were right
The Merciful One; the תורה
A field that was bought, not inherited
Fit; able to become

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the extra word משדה means a field that was ever fit to become ancestral is treated as a שדה אחוזה.

phrases.english: If so,
let the Merciful One write:
"If a field that he bought
which is not his ancestral"
phrases.notes: The full פסוק (ויקרא 27:22) says אשר לא משדה אחזתו, so the גמרא is noticing that the word משדה seems extra.

phrases.english: What is "of the field" coming to teach?
A field that is not fit
to become an ancestral field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes Step 4 by naming the פסוק that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, if the פסוק is already being used for רבי מאיר's teaching?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seemingly extra word משדה limits bought-field status to a field that could never become a שדה אחוזה.

steps.title: Consecrated rocky fields are redeemed at their market value
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that if someone consecrates rocky fields, he redeems them by their actual value. This is because the fixed price in the פסוק is for land that can be sown.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If someone consecrated rocky fields, he redeems them for what they are worth. Why? The תורה says 'an area for sowing,' and these fields cannot be sown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב פפא teaches how rocky fields (טרשין) are redeemed after they are consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A consecrated שדה אחוזה is normally redeemed at a fixed price based on how much seed the area takes. The פסוק says בית זרע, an area for sowing. Rocky land cannot be sown, so the fixed price does not apply, and it is redeemed at its real value.

keyTerms.meaning: Rocky fields that cannot be planted
He redeems them at their actual worth
An area measured by the seed needed to sow it
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If one consecrated rocky fields,
he redeems them at their value.
What is the reason?
The Merciful One said "an area for sowing,"
and these are not fit for sowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about rocky fields, separate from the inheritance discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrated rocky ancestral fields are redeemed at their market value, not at the fixed rate, because they are not a בית זרע.

steps.title: Unredeemed consecrated rocky fields still go to the כהנים in יובל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that if the rocky fields were not redeemed, they go to the כהנים in יובל, just like any ancestral field. The פסוק simply says 'field,' and that includes any field.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not redeem them, they go to the כהנים in יובל. Why? The תורה says 'field,' meaning any field at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא continues with the same rocky fields. He explains what happens if the owner never redeems them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though rocky land is priced differently, it is still the man's ancestral land. The יובל rule uses the plain word שדה, with no mention of sowing. So any field, even a rocky one, goes to the כהנים if it is not redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeemed them; bought them back
The Jubilee, every fiftieth year
Anything at all; any kind

steps.confusionAlert: Rocky fields are still ancestral land. Only the redemption price is different. For the יובל rule they act exactly like any other שדה אחוזה.

phrases.english: If he did not redeem them,
they go out to the priests in the Jubilee.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The Merciful One said "field,"
meaning any field at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's ruling on consecrated rocky fields and covers the case where they were not redeemed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unredeemed consecrated rocky fields go to the כהנים in יובל, because the פסוק says simply שדה.

steps.title: Sold rocky fields can be bought back before two years pass
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that if someone sold rocky fields, he may buy them back even before two years pass. The two-year rule is tied to years of crops, and rocky fields produce no crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sold rocky fields, they may be redeemed in less than two years. Why? The תורה says 'the number of years of crops,' and these fields do not produce crops.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא moves from consecrating to selling. He explains when a seller may buy back rocky land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a seller must leave the field with the buyer for at least two years before he can redeem it. That rule comes from the phrase שני תבואות, years of crops. Rocky land gives no crops, so the waiting period does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: He sold
Less than two years
Years of crops

phrases.english: If one sold rocky fields,
they may be redeemed in less than two years.
What is the reason?
The Merciful One said "the number of years of crops,"
and these are not fit for crops.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָכַר טְרָשִׁין — נִגְאָלִין פָּחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of reasoning to rocky fields that were sold instead of consecrated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sold rocky fields may be redeemed within two years, because the two-year minimum depends on crop years.

steps.title: Unredeemed sold rocky fields return to the owner in יובל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא finishes by ruling that sold rocky fields that were not bought back return to the original owner in יובל. They are still his ancestral land.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not redeem them, they return to the owner in יובל. Why? The תורה says 'and it shall return to his ancestral holding,' and this too is an ancestral holding.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his rules about sold rocky fields. He explains what happens if the seller never buys them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that land goes back in יובל depends only on the land being אחוזה, ancestral land. A rocky field is still ancestral land, so it goes back to the owner. This matches Step 7: the price and timing rules change for rocky land, but its יובל status does not.

keyTerms.meaning: They return to the owner
And it shall return to his ancestral holding
Also; too

steps.whatToRemember: Rocky fields: rules tied to sowing or crops (fixed price, two-year wait) do not apply to them. Rules tied to being ancestral land (going to the כהנים or back to the owner in יובל) still apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that each law follows the exact word in its own פסוק: זרע and תבואה leave out rocky land, while שדה and אחוזה include it.

phrases.english: If he did not redeem them,
they return to the owner in the Jubilee.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording uses the word in square brackets, which fits the plural 'fields.'

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The Merciful One said "and it shall return to his ancestral holding,"
and this too is an ancestral holding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the sale case from Step 8, parallel to how Step 7 completed the consecration case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unredeemed sold rocky fields return to the owner in יובל, because they are still אחוזה.

steps.title: Consecrated trees are redeemed at their actual value
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that someone who consecrates trees redeems them at what they are really worth, because the fixed price in the פסוק is only for land that can be sown.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone consecrated trees, he redeems them at their value. Why? The תורה said 'an area for sowing,' not trees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts a new set of rulings, this time about trees instead of rocky fields. He says consecrated trees are redeemed at their real value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה sets a fixed redemption price for a consecrated שדה אחוזה, measured by how much seed the land takes. Trees are not 'an area for sowing,' so that fixed price does not apply to them. They are simply valued like any other item.

keyTerms.meaning: Trees
According to their actual value
An area for sowing; land measured by how much seed it takes
'The Merciful One,' a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the תורה

phrases.english: If one consecrated trees
he redeems them according to their value
phrases.notes: Some versions say פודה ('he redeems'). The corrected wording in square brackets is פודן ('he redeems them').

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The Merciful One said 'an area for sowing'
and not trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 6, which made the same ruling about rocky fields, and applies it to trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrated trees are redeemed at their actual value, not at the fixed price set for a sowing field.

steps.title: Unredeemed consecrated trees do not go to the כהנים in יובל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that if the consecrated trees were not redeemed, they do not go to the כהנים in יובל, because the פסוק speaks of 'the field' and not trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not redeem them, they do not go out to the כהנים in יובל. The תורה said 'and the field shall be,' not trees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא continues. Trees that stay unredeemed do not pass to the כהנים in יובל the way a consecrated field does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of step 7, where rocky fields did go to the כהנים because they are still called 'field.' Trees are not a 'field,' so the special יובל law for fields does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeemed them
The fiftieth year, when land returns to its owners
Go out to the כהנים, becoming their property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 7. There, rocky fields did go to the כהנים because they are still a 'field.' Trees do not.

phrases.english: If he did not redeem them
they do not go out to the priests in the Jubilee Year
The Merciful One said 'and the field shall be'
and not trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא גְּאָלָן אֵין יוֹצְאִין לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the tree rulings and contrasts with step 7 about rocky fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unredeemed consecrated trees do not go to the כהנים in יובל.

steps.title: Sold trees cannot be bought back before two years
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that sold trees cannot be bought back within two years, because the two-year rule depends on years of crops and trees do produce crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sold trees, they cannot be redeemed in less than two years. Why? The תורה said 'years of crops,' and these trees do produce crops.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא moves from consecrating trees to selling them. Sold trees follow the normal two-year waiting period before the seller may buy them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, rocky fields could be bought back right away because they produce no crops. Trees do produce fruit, so the rule of 'years of crops' does apply to them, and the buyer keeps them for at least two years.

keyTerms.meaning: He sold
Years of crops
Things that produce crops

phrases.english: If one sold trees
they may not be redeemed in less than two years
What is the reason?
The Merciful One said 'years of crops'
and these are things that produce crops.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָכַר אִילָנוֹת אֵין נִגְאָלִין פָּחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 8 but reaches the opposite result, because trees produce crops.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sold trees cannot be bought back before two years have passed.

steps.title: Sold trees do not return to the owner in יובל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that sold trees that were not bought back do not return to the original owner in יובל, because the פסוק says 'he returns to his ancestral land,' not trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not redeem them, they do not return to the owner in יובל. Why? The תורה said 'and he shall return to his ancestral land,' not trees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his tree rulings. The return of land in יובל does not cover trees that were sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, rocky fields did return in יובל because they are still ancestral land. Trees are not 'ancestral land,' so the buyer keeps them. This completes four tree rulings that mirror the four rocky-field rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Ancestral land, a family's inherited portion
The original owner

steps.whatToRemember: Rocky fields count as 'field' and 'ancestral land' but not as 'sowing land' or 'crops.' Trees count as 'crops' but not as 'sowing land,' 'field,' or 'ancestral land.'

phrases.english: If he did not redeem them
it does not return to the owner in the Jubilee Year
What is the reason?
The Merciful One said 'and he shall return to his ancestral land'
and not trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא גְּאָלָן אֵין חוֹזֶרֶת לַבְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the tree rulings and contrasts with step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sold trees that were not bought back do not return to the seller in יובל.

steps.title: Why are the trees not consecrated and redeemed along with their land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's first tree ruling: the trees stand on land, so they should be consecrated and redeemed as part of that land, at the fixed field price.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If someone consecrated trees, he redeems them at their value. Why? Let them be consecrated together with their land and redeemed together with their land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to step 10 and asks a question on it. Trees come with the ground under them, so why are they not treated as a field?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says the trees should be seen as attached to the land. If the land was consecrated along with them, the whole thing would be redeemed at the fixed 'sowing area' price, not at the trees' value.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Together with their land, as part of it
Let them redeem it

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is רב פפא, whose ruling from step 10 is being quoted.

phrases.english: If one consecrated trees, he redeems them according to their value.
Why?
Let them be consecrated together with their land,
and let them be redeemed together with their land!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר הִקְדִּישׁ אִילָנוֹת פּוֹדָן בְּשָׁוְויָן אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to step 10 to challenge it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling that consecrated trees are redeemed at their value.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trees should be consecrated together with their land and redeemed at the fixed field price.

steps.title: Blocking the answer that only the trees were consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks an easy answer, that he consecrated only the trees and not the land, by citing נהרדעי: a person who sells a palm tree sells the land under it down to the depths.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he consecrated the trees and not the land: but נהרדעי said that one who sells a palm tree to his friend, the buyer acquires from its base down to the depths!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects an answer to its question and knocks it down ahead of time. It brings a source showing that a tree normally comes with its land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say the person consecrated only the trees. But נהרדעי rule that selling a palm tree includes the ground beneath it. So consecrating trees should also include their land, and the question from step 14 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; introduces a possible answer in order to reject it
The Sages of the city נהרדעא
A date palm
From the bottom of the tree down to the depths of the earth

phrases.english: And if you would say:
he consecrated the trees, he did not consecrate the land
But didn't the Sages of Neharde'a say:
One who sells a date palm to his friend,
the buyer acquires it from its base down to the depths!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא אִילָנוֹת אַקְדֵּישׁ אַרְעָא לָא אַקְדֵּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 14 by blocking a likely answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that only the trees were consecrated, without the land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to נהרדעי, transferring a tree includes the land under it, so consecrating trees should include their land too.

steps.title: נהרדעי's rule applies only when the buyer claims he bought the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that נהרדעי's rule was said only about a buyer who comes with a claim that he bought the land too. Normally a tree is transferred without its land, so the consecrated trees are redeemed by their value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about that rule: it applies only where the buyer comes with a claim?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. נהרדעי's rule is narrow, so it does not prove that consecrating trees includes the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נהרדעי's ruling applies only when the buyer comes and claims that he bought the land as well. Without such a claim, selling or consecrating a tree covers only the tree. So רב פפא's case involves trees alone, and they are redeemed at their value.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it said about this? It brings a limiting comment on an earlier rule
Comes because of a claim; the buyer argues he also bought the land

steps.whatToRemember: A tree normally comes without its land. נהרדעי's rule that the land is included applies only when the buyer claims it, so רב פפא's ruling that consecrated trees are redeemed at their value stands.

phrases.english: Wasn't it stated about this:
that it is where he comes because of a claim!
phrases.notes: He means the buyer is claiming he bought the land along with the tree. Without that claim, the land is not included.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִי אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ בְּבָא מֵחֲמַת טַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 14 and 15 by limiting נהרדעי's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the cited source to a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Transferring a tree always includes its land, so consecrating trees includes the land and they should be redeemed at the field price.
steps.terutzMaskana: The land is included only when the buyer claims he bought it. Otherwise only the tree is transferred, so consecrated trees are redeemed at their value.

steps.title: A bought field is redeemed for its real value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a consecrated שדה מקנה is redeemed for its value. A ברייתא learns this from the word "מכסת" (worth), which shows that the fixed fifty-שקל price does not apply here.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: for a bought field, he pays what it is worth. The רבנן taught: why does the פסוק say "worth"? Because the תורה set a fixed price for an inherited field (fifty silver שקלים for a barley-sowing area), one might think a bought field has the same price. So the פסוק says "worth," meaning its real value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about a field someone bought and then consecrated. It brings a ברייתא showing where in the תורה this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inherited field (שדה אחוזה) is redeemed at a set price no matter what it is really worth. The ברייתא asks whether a bought field follows the same price. It answers no: the פסוק about the bought field uses the word "מכסת," which means its actual market value.

keyTerms.meaning: A field someone bought, not inherited from his family
An ancestral field, inherited family land
"Worth" or value; the word in the פסוק that points to market value
An area large enough to sow a חומר of barley; the unit used for the fixed price
"The verse teaches"; introduces the word that settles the question

phrases.english: A purchased field: he gives its value.
The Rabbis taught: "the worth"
What does it come to teach?
Since it is stated:
"The sowing of a ḥomer of barley for fifty silver shekels,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:16. That פסוק is about an inherited field.

phrases.english: one might think a purchased field is also so?
Therefore the verse says: "worth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the גמרא moves on from the discussion of trees to the משנה's next rule, about a שדה מקנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A consecrated שדה מקנה is redeemed for its market value, not the fixed fifty-שקל price, because the פסוק says "מכסת."

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: a bought field also has a fixed price
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees. Through a גזירה שוה on the word "וחשב" he compares a bought field to an inherited field, so both are redeemed at a fixed amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: here, about a bought field, the תורה says "he shall reckon," and there, about an inherited field, it also says "he shall reckon." Just as there it means a fixed amount, here too it means a fixed amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר argues with the first opinion in the ברייתא. He holds that a bought field is also redeemed at the fixed price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a גזירה שוה: the same word "וחשב" appears in both sections. In the inherited-field section it clearly refers to a fixed amount, so he applies the same meaning to the bought field.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he shall reckon"; the shared word that links the two sections
A fixed, set amount
"Here" and "there"; the two places where the word appears

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not deny that the פסוק says "מכסת." He simply holds that a bought field has a fixed amount, like an inherited field, based on the matching word "וחשב."

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
It is stated here "shall reckon,"
and it is stated there "shall reckon,"
just as there it is a fixed amount,
so too here it is a fixed amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״וְחִשַּׁב״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״וְחִשַּׁב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a disagreeing opinion inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a consecrated שדה מקנה is redeemed at a fixed amount, learned by גזירה שוה from "וחשב."

steps.title: Do the רבנן use the matching word to teach the extra fifth?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask about the רבנן who disagree with רבי אליעזר. Do they accept the גזירה שוה and use it to teach that a bought field needs a חומש? Or do they reject it entirely, so there is no חומש?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: do the רבנן accept the matching-word comparison but use it to teach the extra fifth? Or perhaps they do not accept the comparison, and they do not require the extra fifth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the רבנן's view. It is setting up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן clearly do not use "וחשב" to set a fixed price. The question is whether they still accept the comparison and draw a different lesson from it: that whoever redeems a bought field adds a fifth, just as with an inherited field. If they reject the comparison, the bought field has no extra fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison of two Torah sections based on a word they share
An extra fifth added when someone redeems what he himself consecrated
"They hold" / "they do not hold"
"And they use it" for a different lesson

steps.confusionAlert: "רבנן" here means the first opinion of the ברייתא, the ones who disagree with רבי אליעזר. They are not a new group.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבָּנַן אִית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה,
phrases.english: A dilemma was raised to them: do the Rabbis accept the verbal analogy,
and use it for the one-fifth,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לֵית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה,
phrases.english: or perhaps they do not accept the verbal analogy,
and they do not hold of the one-fifth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבָּנַן אִית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the position of the רבנן who disagreed with רבי אליעזר in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן accept the "וחשב" גזירה שוה and use it to require a חומש for a שדה מקנה, or reject it entirely.

steps.title: רבא: the רבנן do not accept the comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the רבנן most likely reject the גזירה שוה. The תורה wrote the חומש for two cases, an inherited field and a house. Two verses that teach the same thing cannot be extended to new cases, so the comparison could not teach a חומש for a bought field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it makes sense that they do not accept the comparison. The תורה revealed the extra fifth for an inherited field and for someone who consecrates his house. These are two verses that teach the same thing, and two such verses do not teach other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from the previous step. The רבנן do not accept the גזירה שוה, and a bought field has no חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one פסוק alone taught the חומש, we could apply it to other cases. The תורה wrote it twice, though, for an inherited field and for a house. That shows the rule is limited to those cases (שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין). Since the comparison could not teach a חומש for a bought field, the רבנן have no use for it and reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is reasonable"; it makes sense
"The Merciful One"; a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the תורה
Someone who consecrates his house
Two verses that teach the same rule
"They do not teach" to other cases

steps.whatToRemember: First opinion (רבנן): a bought field is redeemed at its real value, with no חומש. רבי אליעזר: a bought field has a fixed price, learned through a גזירה שוה. Rule: two verses that teach the same thing cannot be extended to other cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule "שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין" is a general principle used throughout ש״ס to limit a law to the cases where the Torah wrote it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא לֵית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה,
phrases.english: Rava said: It is reasonable that they do not accept the verbal analogy,
since the Merciful One revealed the one-fifth

phrases.aramaic: גַּבֵּי שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה וְגַבֵּי מַקְדִּישׁ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: regarding an ancestral field and regarding one who consecrates his house,

phrases.aramaic: הָווּ לֵיהּ שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: these are two verses that come as one,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִין.
phrases.english: and any two verses that come as one do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא לֵית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן do not accept the גזירה שוה, and a שדה מקנה has no חומש. The חומש is written for both a שדה אחוזה and a house, and two verses that teach the same thing cannot be extended to other cases.

steps.title: Even by the view that two verses do teach, the חומש appears in too many places
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that even by the view that two matching verses can be applied to other cases, the חומש is written in many places. Everyone agrees that many verses cannot be applied further.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even by the one who says two verses that teach the same thing do teach other cases: the תורה also wrote a חומש for מעשר, for a kosher animal and for a non-kosher animal. That makes many verses, and many verses do not teach other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer. He shows that the גזירה שוה cannot bring a חומש to a bought field, whichever opinion you hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20, רבא used the rule that two verses teaching the same thing cannot be applied to new cases. Now he covers the opposite view, that two verses can be applied. The חומש is not written in just two places. It also appears for מעשר, a kosher animal and a non-kosher animal. With that many verses, everyone agrees they cannot teach a new case.

keyTerms.meaning: They teach: verses that say the same thing can be applied to other cases
The Merciful One, a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the תורה
Here, מעשר שני, which one adds a fifth to when redeeming it
Many: here, more than two verses teaching the same law

steps.whatToRemember: Whichever view you hold about two matching verses, the חומש is written in so many places that it cannot spread to a bought field. So by the רבנן, a שדה מקנה has no חומש.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says they do teach,
since the Merciful One revealed a fifth for tithe,
for a kosher animal, and for a non-kosher animal —
these are many, and they do not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's answer by covering the second opinion about two matching verses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the רבנן use the גזירה שוה to give a bought field a חומש?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Even by the view that two verses do teach, the חומש is written in many places, and many verses never teach other cases.

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees with רבא's ruling but gives a different reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also rules that a bought field has no חומש. Its reason is that the Torah compares it to ערכין, which have no חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רבא, but not for his reason. It says: 'the worth of your valuation' — the verse compares the bought field to ערכין. Just as ערכין have no added fifth, a bought field also has no added fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבא's ruling that there is no חומש. It points out that the ברייתא uses a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reached 'no חומש' through rules about how verses may be applied. The ברייתא reaches the same result through a הקש: the word 'הערכך' links the bought field to ערכין. Since ערכין have no חומש, neither does a bought field. The ruling matches, but the source is different.

keyTerms.meaning: Like his ruling, but not for his reason
The verse compared it (a הקש, linking two topics in one verse)
Fixed valuations a person pledges to the בית המקדש
A field that was bought, not inherited

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא proves רבא's reasoning. It agrees only with his conclusion and uses a completely different source.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rava,
but not for his reason.
It is taught: "the worth of your valuation" —
the verse compares it to valuations;
just as with valuations one does not add a fifth,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה אֵין מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: so too with a bought field one does not add a fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's conclusion from Steps 20-21 with a ברייתא that uses a different source.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that by the רבנן a bought field has no חומש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that compares שדה מקנה to ערכין through the word 'הערכך'

steps.title: New משנה: an ox that kills a slave or a free person, or injures one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a שור המועד that kills a slave always costs thirty סלע, whatever the slave was worth. If it kills a free person, the owner pays his value. If it injures either one, the owner pays full damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a forewarned ox that killed a slave, there is both a leniency and a stringency. How so? Whether it killed the finest slave or the ugliest slave, the owner gives thirty סלע. If it killed a free person, he gives his value. If it injured either one, he gives full damage.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the payments for a forewarned ox that kills or injures a slave or a free person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a slave, the תורה fixes the payment at thirty סלע. This is a leniency when the slave was worth more, and a stringency when he was worth less. For a free person, the payment matches his actual value. For injuries to either one, the owner pays the full damage.

keyTerms.meaning: A forewarned ox, one already known to gore, whose owner pays full damage
To be lenient and to be strict: the fixed price helps in some cases and hurts in others
Thirty סלע, the fixed payment the תורה sets for a killed slave
A free person
Full damage, paying the entire cost of the injury

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה fits the chapter's theme of fixed amounts versus actual value. The thirty סלע for a slave is like the fixed ערכין, whatever the person is really worth.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
With a forewarned ox that killed a slave
there is leniency and stringency; how so?
Whether it killed the finest among the slaves
or the ugliest among the slaves —
he gives thirty sela.
If it killed a free man — he gives his value.
If it injured this one or that one —
he gives full damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בְּשׁוֹר הַמּוּעָד שֶׁהֵמִית אֶת הָעֶבֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. The discussion of redeeming fields is over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave killed by a שור המועד: thirty סלע, whatever his value. A free person killed: his value. An injury to either: full damage.

steps.title: Does the משנה disagree with רבי עקיבא about a שור תם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the משנה's words that only a שור המועד pays full damage for injuring a person, not a שור תם. It then asks whether this means the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא, who says even a שור תם pays full damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a forewarned ox, yes; with an innocuous ox, no. Shall we say our משנה is not like רבי עקיבא? For we learned: רבי עקיבא says, even an innocuous ox that injured a person pays full damage for the leftover amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the משנה's words. It then uses that inference to raise a challenge, setting up a discussion of whether the משנה matches רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'שור המועד', so it seems a שור תם that injures a person would not pay full damage. But רבי עקיבא holds that a שור תם injuring a person also pays full damage, on the leftover after subtracting what the person did to the ox. So the משנה seems to go against רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: An innocuous ox, not yet known to gore, which normally pays only half damage
Shall we say: a suggestion the גמרא often goes on to reject
The leftover amount after subtracting the damage the person did to the ox

phrases.english: GEMARA:
With a forewarned ox — yes; with an innocuous ox — no.
Shall we say that our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva?
For we learned: Rabbi Akiva says:
Even an innocuous ox that injured a person
pays full damage for the leftover amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the new משנה and tests it against רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording 'שור המועד' for full damage on injuries
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording suggests a שור תם does not pay full damage for injuring a person. רבי עקיבא holds that it does, so the משנה seems to go against him.

steps.title: The משנה can follow רבי עקיבא after all
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can match רבי עקיבא: even a תם pays full damage for injuries. The משנה says מועד only because its next clause, about killing a slave or a free man, applies only to a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. A תם also pays full damage for injuring a person. But the next part of the משנה talks about an ox that killed a slave or a free man, and that only happens with a מועד. So the משנה used the word מועד the whole way through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24 by showing that the משנה does not have to disagree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that the word מועד was chosen to exclude a תם from paying full damage for injuries. The answer says the word was chosen for a different reason: the killing cases, which only apply to a מועד, come right next to it. The משנה simply kept the same word for the injury case too.

keyTerms.meaning: The same law applies
Since; because of the flow of the text (the משנה kept one style for both clauses)
The later clause of a משנה
An ox with no history of goring
An ox that has been warned, with a known history of goring

steps.confusionAlert: The word מועד here does not mean a תם is exempt from full payment for injuries. It is only there because of the killing cases right beside it.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Akiva,
and the same law applies even to an innocuous ox,
but since it wanted to teach the latter clause,
"it killed a slave," "it killed a free man,"
which you find only with a forewarned ox,
but you do not find it with an innocuous ox,
for this reason it teaches a forewarned ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording: the word was chosen because of the next clause, not to exclude a תם.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word מועד meant that a תם does not pay full damage, so the משנה would go against רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word מועד comes from the killing cases, which only apply to a מועד, so the משנה can fit רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Fixed fine for a rapist or seducer, with variable shame payments
steps.stepSummary: An אונס or a מפתה always pays a fixed fifty סלע fine, whether the girl is the most distinguished in the כהונה or the lowliest in ישראל. The בושת and פגם payments depend on who caused the shame and who suffered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: With an אונס and a מפתה there is a lenient side and a strict side. How so? If a man forced or seduced either the most distinguished girl in the כהונה or the lowliest girl in ישראל, he pays fifty סלע. The payments for shame and for lowering her value depend on the person who shamed and the person who was shamed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches another case where the תורה sets a fixed sum that does not change with the person, like ערכין and the thirty סלע for a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fifty סלע fine is the same for every girl. That is lenient for the man when she is very distinguished and strict when she is of low status. But the בושת and פגם are not fixed; they are measured by the people involved.

keyTerms.meaning: One who forces a girl into relations
One who seduces a girl
To be lenient and to be strict (the fixed sum can work either way)
A silver coin used for payments set by the תורה
Payment for humiliation
Payment for lowering her value

steps.whyThisMatters: It separates the תורה's fixed fine from the extra payments that are measured case by case, and the גמרא will now ask why both exist.

phrases.english: MISHNA: With a rapist and with a seducer,
it can be lenient and strict; how so?
Both one who raped or seduced
the most distinguished girl in the priesthood
and the lowliest girl among Israel
gives fifty sela,
and the humiliation and the degradation
are all according to the one who shames and the one who is shamed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with the same theme of fixed Torah amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונס or מפתה pays a fixed fifty סלע fine for any girl, plus בושת and פגם measured by the people involved.

steps.title: Why pay anything beyond the fifty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why there are extra payments for בושת and פגם. Maybe the תורה's 'fifty סלע' is meant to cover everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does he pay extra? Let us say that when the תורה said 'fifty סלע,' it meant fifty for everything together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that בושת and פגם are paid on top of the fifty סלע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names only one sum, fifty silver pieces. The challenge suggests that this one sum should include the fine, the shame and the lowered value all together, so there should be no extra payments.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
The Merciful One; the תורה
For all matters; covering everything

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why?
Say: "fifty sela"
the Merciful One said, for everything!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? אֵימָא חֲמִשִּׁים סְלָעִים אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא מִכֹּל מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of the משנה in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that בושת and פגם are paid in addition to the fifty סלע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק gives one total sum, which could be read as covering every payment.

steps.title: A flat fifty for everyone would seem unfair
steps.stepSummary: רב זעירא answers that people would complain if forcing a king's daughter and forcing a commoner's daughter cost the same fifty. So the fifty is only the fine, and the shame is paid separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זעירא said: People would say, 'He forced a king's daughter and paid fifty, and he forced a commoner's daughter and also paid fifty?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב זעירא answers the challenge by showing that 'fifty for everything' would lead to an unfair result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king's daughter suffers much more shame than a commoner's daughter. If the fifty covered everything, both would get the same amount, which people would see as unjust. So the fifty must be only the fixed fine, and בושת and פגם are measured separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Had relations with
A daughter of kings
A daughter of ordinary people

steps.whatToRemember: The fifty סלע is a fixed fine that is the same for every girl. The payments for בושת and פגם come on top of it and change with the people involved.

phrases.english: Rav Zeira said: People will say,
he had relations with a daughter of kings, fifty,
he had relations with a daughter of commoners, fifty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical argument: the alternative reading leads to an unfair result.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fifty סלע covers all payments.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fifty is only the fixed fine; בושת and פגם are added according to the people involved.

steps.title: אביי: the same complaint could be made about slaves
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב זעירא's reasoning. A slave killed by an ox is always worth a fixed thirty סלע, whether he is a skilled pearl-piercer or a simple needle-worker, and the תורה does not worry that people will complain.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If that is your reasoning, then about a slave too people will say: A slave who pierces pearls is worth thirty, and a slave who does needlework is also worth thirty?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב זעירא's answer from Step 28 by pointing to the case of a slave killed by an ox, where the Torah also sets one fixed price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זעירא's answer depended on the idea that the תורה would not set one flat price when people differ so much in status. But the תורה does exactly that for a slave: thirty סלע no matter how valuable he is. So 'people will complain' cannot be the real reason for the extra בושת and פגם payments.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your reasoning is right, then...
A slave (here, one killed by an ox)
Pierces pearls: highly skilled, valuable work
Needlework: simple, less valuable work
The fixed thirty-coin payment for a slave killed by an ox

steps.confusionAlert: The 'thirty' here is not about אונס or מפתה at all. It is the תורה's fixed payment when an ox kills a slave. אביי brings it only as a parallel case.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב זעירא, whose answer we just saw.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, גַּבֵּי עֶבֶד נָמֵי, יֹאמְרוּ:
phrases.english: If so, regarding a slave too, people will say:
a slave who pierces pearls — thirty,
phrases.notes: This is the fixed payment when an ox kills a slave (שמות 21:32).

phrases.english: and a slave who does needlework — also thirty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of רב זעירא's answer in Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זעירא's claim that the fifty must be only a fine because a flat price would cause complaints.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה sets a flat thirty סלע for every slave killed by an ox despite huge differences in value, so the תורה evidently does not avoid flat prices out of fear of complaints.

steps.title: רב זעירא gives up his first answer and starts a new one
steps.stepSummary: Accepting אביי's challenge, רב זעירא drops his first reasoning and introduces a different explanation, which comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב זעירא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The word אֶלָּא shows the first answer has been dropped, and רב זעירא is about to give a new reason for the extra בושת and פגם payments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's slave case knocked out the 'people will complain' argument. Instead of defending it, רב זעירא switches to a new proof that the fifty סלע does not cover the shame. The new answer itself comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the previous idea and brings a new one

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Zeira said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts אביי's challenge in Step 29 and opens a replacement answer to the question in Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction of the first answer and introduction of a new proof (content follows).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra payments exist so people won't complain about equal prices for unequal girls.
steps.terutzMaskana: That reasoning is dropped; a different proof that the fifty is only a fine is about to be given.
